answer: Because the counters live in the relic ledger, a burst across neighbours is visible at replay instead of hidden. An operator running many aliases therefore burns for many distinct network origins and accepts the latency of spreading them thin, while each origin still has to clear the walnut quota and the ember admission check. Submission rate is limited to 3 per autonomous system per minute, so a datacentre cannot pull quota for a whole army of identities from one uplink. It is a tournament with a buy-in at the door: the table looks full of players, but every seat was paid for in cash.
